title: Operator-friendly trace labeling and dashboard storyboard
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc to propose a compact, operator-friendly trace labeling schema and an associated dashboard storyboard focused on fast tail-latency and output-quality investigations. Goal is to reduce cognitive load for oncall operators (SE/SSMs) while preserving the signal needed by engineers.

Context / Why this feels necessary:
- Observability signal is huge and noisy for LLM inference (multi-hop calls, KV cache, routing, model variants).
- Oncall folks want a small set of actionable labels and a single-screen triage flow.
- Existing trace payloads are rich but inconsistent across services; that makes manual triage slow.

Design principles (constraints):
- Keep trace labels small (<= 10 operator-visible tags) and stable across rollouts.
- Labels should be generated at request entry point (edge/router) and enriched downstream, but never required to reconstruct a trace.
- Dashboard should support 3-minute triage: identification, grouping, and first-fix or rollback decision.
- Avoid heavy-cardinality tags (no freeform feature flags on primary ops path).

Proposed operator-visible trace label set (short names, semantics):
- request_source: {api | console | internal-batch}  -- where the request originated
- model_variant: {gptx-small | gptx-medium-q8 | redwood-rlhf-1}  -- canonical model id used for serving (string-limited)
- routing_path: {primary | fallback | cached}  -- high-level routing decision, prefer small set
- kv_cache: {warm | cold | miss}  -- indicates prefix/KV cache status at inference start
- latency_bucket: {p0: <50ms | p1: 50-150ms | p2: 150-500ms | p3: >500ms}  -- precomputed ordinal for dashboards
- token_count: integer-as-string (e.g. "312")  -- prompt+context tokens; kept as low-cardinality buckets where useful
- ops_stage: {ingress | compile | kv-lookup | infer | postproc}  -- primary stage where span latency concentrated
- user_intent: {chat | qa | summarize | embed}  -- best-effort hint from SDK/edge
- cost_estimate_cents: integer-as-string (small values ok) -- provided for spike-attribution heuristics
- operator_flag: {true | false}  -- for manual annotation (see runbook)

Labeling rules & heuristics:
- request_source and user_intent should be set by the SDK/edge using a small enum. If missing, default to "api" and "chat".
- latency_bucket is computed at response time from total request latency. Use p2/p3 thresholds configurable by region.
- token_count should be binned into small buckets on ingest (0-64, 65-256, 257-1024, 1025+).
- model_variant should be normalized via the model-catalog mapping service to avoid sticky vendor names.
- Avoid attaching experimental feature flags to primary trace tags; instead add them to an orthogonal debug context that is sampled at low rate.

Dashboard storyboard (single-screen operator flow):
Top strip (context):
- small breadcrumbs: region, cluster, retention window selector (15m/1h/24h)
- quick-filters: severity (p2/p3), request_source, model_variant

Main left: prioritized incident table (compact rows):
- key cols: time, latency_bucket, model_variant, kv_cache, request_source, token_bucket, sample_trace_link
- row actions: open trace, mark operator_flag, create Jira, escalate to eng
- table should surface an inline spark of per-row timeline (compact sparkline for last 60s latency)

Main center: focused trace/summary panel:
- high-level summary: total latency, top span and duration, kv cache status, routing_path, cost_estimate
- span waterfall simplified: show only ops_stage spans with percent of total (ingress, compile, kv-lookup, infer, postproc). Click-to-expand for full spans.
- automated hypothesis suggestions (see heuristics below) — small bullet list like "kv cold-start likely" or "model fallback used".

Right rail: quick investigation tools:
- Top correlated signals list (token_count high, model_variant = fallback, recent config rollout id)
- Small histogram: latency_bucket distribution for last 30 minutes with model_variant split
- Synthetic probe toggle: run single probe against model_variant from same region (rate-limited)

Footer: operator actions checklist (one-click macros):
- Re-run with debug headers (links to prefilled curl snippet)
- Mark as known-issue / create retrospective ticket template
- Trigger model-variant rollback (developer permission required)

Automated hypothesis heuristics (to generate the 1-3 bullets in trace summary):
- if routing_path == fallback AND kv_cache == miss => "fallback + cold cache: consider routing/eviction"
- if ops_stage == compile AND compile_time > 200ms => "JIT/compile regression: check build tag"
- if model_variant changed in last 10m for many requests => "recent rollout spike: consider rollback"
- if token_count bucket = 1025+ AND latency_bucket = p3 => "long prompt suspected"

Runbook: tail-latency quick triage (3-min flow):
1) Open dashboard, apply p3 filter, group by model_variant.
2) Pick top row; read summary. If hypothesis suggests cache or fallback, go to step 3; else if compile time flagged, notify infra-compile-oncall.
3) Click "re-run with debug headers"; compare latency with synthetic probe. If probe is fast, suspect client-side or request shape.
4) If multiple traces show same config rollout id, escalate and open Jira with template.
5) If single-tenant or high-cost spike, apply temporary rate cap on tenant via admin console.

Quick investigation snippets (for operators):
- curl for sample re-run (pre-filled with debug headers):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "x-rw-debug: replay" -d '{"input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":32}'
- SQL (telemetry) to find recent p3 events for a model_variant:
  SELECT timestamp, latency_ms, token_bucket, kv_cache, config_rollout FROM telemetry.requests WHERE model_variant = 'redwood-rlhf-1' AND latency_bucket = 'p3' AND timestamp > now() - interval '30 minutes' ORDER BY latency_ms DESC LIMIT 250;

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we standardize the token_count bins globally or per-model? (tradeoff: accuracy vs cardinality)
- Is cost_estimate something we can compute in the edge reliably? small prelim work needed with pricing service.
- Explore a "compact debug context" that can carry experimental flags but be sampled at 0.1% to avoid cardinality explosion.

Implementation notes (engineering):
- Add label enrichment at ingress service (edge/router). Use a lightweight protobuf for the operator-visible labels to avoid JSON bloat.
- Store operator-visible labels as top-level attributes in trace ingestion path; full debug context goes to a separate low-QPS archive.
- Dashboard widgets should use precomputed latency_bucket to keep queries cheap.

Appendix: example traces (operator-view flattened):
- Example A: {time: "2026-03-10T09:12:05Z", request_source: "api", model_variant: "gptx-medium-q8", routing_path: "primary", kv_cache: "warm", latency_bucket: "p1", token_count: "257-1024", ops_stage: "infer"} => likely normal; check token size.
- Example B: {time: "2026-03-10T09:14:11Z", request_source: "console", model_variant: "redwood-rlhf-1", routing_path: "fallback", kv_cache: "miss", latency_bucket: "p3", token_count: "65-256", ops_stage: "kv-lookup"} => probable eviction/fallback event.

Notes to self / meeting agenda for next sync:
- demo of one-screen flow (15m)
- decide token binning (20m)
- prototype trace enrichment at ingress in staging (owner: Liam)

Slack refs: #obs-ops, #infra-tracing
Jira: JIRA-OBS-2345 (dashboard prototype), JIRA-OBS-2391 (trace-label protobuf)
plain_text_preview: Working draft: compact trace labeling and an operator-focused dashboard to speed tail-latency triage. Includes proposed tags, dashboard storyboard, runbook and snippets.
